notes: EDA v4: reviewed findings, confidence and rule-input status are in reports/eda/SUMMARY.md and tools/scene/CONTRACT.md. The notes below are automatic descriptive statistics of this clip only.
1298 tracks in 340 s: 770 pedestrians (59%), 458 car, 24 bus, 42 truck, 4 motorcycle, 0 bicycle; 2 person boxes riding two-wheelers were relabelled as riders.
On average 22.2 pedestrians and 29 vehicles are on screen at once (peak 34 pedestrians).

4 vehicle flows found; the largest are F1 middle-right to top-left (right to left, 185 tracks); F2 top-left to bottom-right (towards camera, left to right, 171 tracks); F3 bottom-right to bottom-left (right to left, 10 tracks).

Furthest queued stop that began while head D showed red, red_amber or amber, per flow (rough upper bound for a stop line; D is a timing proxy for the near carriageway only): F1 near [1224, 382] (16% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 1.9 vs 1.6 vehicles while D red vs not red); F2 near [3741, 2158] (61% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 10.4 vs 6.0 vehicles while D red vs not red); F4 near [562, 985] (57% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 0.5 vs 0.1 vehicles while D red vs not red).

Median pedestrian box height is 112 px at 4K; 32% are under 96px (16px at imgsz 640), 3% are under 64px (16px at imgsz 960), 1% are under 48px (16px at imgsz 1280). These are detected boxes, so the smallest people are already missing.

Mean luma goes from 94.8 to 95.1 (+0.4%) over the clip, range 89.1 to 98.1 of 255; the largest swing is +6.1% within 15 s (273 to 288 s). Iris, shutter and gain are constant in the camera metadata (reports/eda/camera), so this is not exposure control; brightness rules (fire_smoke) must still normalise per frame.

167 of 770 pedestrian tracks spend >= 0.5 s on cells used by moving vehicles; 5 crossing corridor(s) found, the busiest spans x 2400 to 3520, y 880 to 1200 (52 people); 53 people are on the road outside corridors, most around [939, 246] (includes kerbside waiting and bus boarding, so an upper bound for jaywalking).

Signal: vehicle head D (3 lamps, from the head inventory) at (2314, 773) in this video; its v4 timeline has a known state for 94.1% of the clip (coverage, not accuracy: no human-verified labels yet). D is a timing proxy for the near-carriageway flow; which movements it controls is unknown.

Of 389 vehicle tracks with enough motion, 328 go straight, 55 turn and 5 reverse heading (U-turn like, e.g. track 10 at [2878, 1259] around 0.0 s); check these by eye before treating them as illegal_u_turn examples.
6 vehicle(s) stand still for over 90% of a track longer than 60 s at [146, 912], [1240, 379], [188, 1053], [72, 824], [1228, 381] (parked), which a stopped_vehicle rule must whitelist or time-gate.
Tracker: 17.5% of tracks live under 1 s and 71.8% of vehicle tracks start away from the frame edge, a sign of occlusion and ID switches.

lane_flow_clustering.method: k-means on start xy, end xy, net heading, then merge clusters that share heading (< 20 deg) and line (< 250 px)
lane_flow_clustering.rule: vehicle tracks >= 2 s and >= 300 px net travel

turning_movements.rule: heading change between first and last 5 moving samples; |d| < 35 straight, > 140 U-turn like; image-plane, so perspective bends it

signal.status: PROVISIONAL (coverage only; no human-verified lamp labels yet)
signal.box_mapping: box_ref (reference C3897 4K px) mapped with H_ref_to_video from registration.json
signal.meaning: head D is a strong timing proxy for the near-carriageway flow; the far carriageway is also cycle-locked with a different phase offset; which movements D physically controls is UNKNOWN (reports/eda/SUMMARY.md, finding 3)

perspective.assumption: person height about 1.7 m; valid only near the fitted y range

pedestrians_on_carriageway.definition: person ground point in a direction-field cell used by moving vehicles, >= 5 samples (~0.5 s)
pedestrians_on_carriageway.corridor_rule: road cells with >= 9 distinct people, dilated by one cell
